{{AI-generated|date=February 2026}}
The '''Kawahara equation''' is a [[partial differential equation]] that arises in various fields of [[mathematical physics]], particularly in the study of wave phenomena. Named after the Japanese mathematician T. Kawahara, who first introduced it in the context of [[fluid dynamics]] and nonlinear wave propagation, this equation extends the well-known [[Korteweg-de Vries equation|Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation]] by incorporating higher-order derivatives. This inclusion allows for the modeling of more complex wave behaviors, capturing phenomena such as wave shape distortion and the emergence of solitary waves in dispersive systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Biswas |first=Anjan |date=2009 |title=Solitary wave solution for the generalized Kawahara equation |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893965908001225 |journal=[[Applied Mathematics Letters]] |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=208–210 |doi=10.1016/j.aml.2008.03.011 |via=Elsevier Science Direct|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Haghighatdoost Gh., M Bazghandi and F. Pashahie |date=2025 |title=A finite generating set of differential invariants for Lie symmetry group of the fifth-order KdV types |url=https://cmde.tabrizu.ac.ir/article_16069.html |journal=Computational Methods for Differential Equations |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=803–810}}</ref>

The Kawahara equation is a fifth-order KdV equation and typically expressed as:<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kawahara |first=T. |date=1972 |title=Oscillatory solitary waves in dispersive media |journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=260–264 |doi=10.1143/JPSJ.33.260 |bibcode=1972JPSJ...33..260K }}</ref>

<math>\partial_t  \phi + \alpha  \phi \partial_x \phi+  \beta \partial_x^3\phi - \gamma\, \partial_x^5 \phi = 0, </math>

where  waves described by function <math>\phi(x,t)</math> and <math>\alpha,\,\beta</math>, and <math>\gamma > 0</math> are constant.
